title: Reading an RNAscope image
objective: Interpret multiplexed RNAscope dots to judge co-expression.

steps.title: Dots, channels, and nuclei
steps.body: Each gene gets its own color channel; each dot is roughly one transcript. **[[DAPI]]** marks nuclei so you can assign dots to cells. **Co-expression** means two colors of dots land inside the *same* cell outline — not just nearby.

steps.prompt: Two probe colors both appear densely in one cell. What does that suggest?
options: The two genes are co-expressed in that cell
The two genes are never expressed together
The two probes are binding the same mRNA
The probes cross-reacted with each other
steps.explanation: Both messages in one cell = co-expression — the basis for defining molecular subtypes.

variants.setup: Red and green dots fill the same neuron, around a single DAPI nucleus.
options: Co-expression of both genes
Mutually exclusive expression
A staining artifact only
variants.reveal: Both channels inside one cell = that cell expresses both genes.

steps.scenario: Red dots are in one set of cells and green dots in a *different*, neighboring set, with almost no overlap.
options: The two genes mark largely separate cell populations
Expression is strictly exclusive in every single cell
The probes compete, so each cell shows only one color
steps.explanation: Separate cells with separate colors = distinct populations. That's a real, useful result — it rules out co-expression.
steps.followUp: This is why you need DAPI and cell outlines: 'nearby' is not 'same cell'.

variants.prompt: Red cells and green cells barely overlap. The two markers are…
options: Marking two largely separate cell populations
Competing, so each cell can show only one color
Both just staining artifacts, nothing real here
variants.explanation: Non-overlap indicates distinct populations, a meaningful result.

steps.setup: You want to prove a new Cre line targets Bmpr1b+ neurons.
options: Show the Cre reporter and Bmpr1b mRNA in the same cells
Show the reporter cells are brighter than their neighbors
Replace the need for any reporter allele whatsoever
Show Bmpr1b mRNA is present somewhere in the DRG
steps.reveal: Co-detecting the **[[reporter]]** and the endogenous marker mRNA in the same cells confirms the line hits the intended subtype — exactly the lab's validation step.

variants.prompt: To confirm a Cre line marks the right subtype, RNAscope can…
options: Show reporter and marker mRNA in the same cells
Show the marker mRNA is present somewhere in DRG
Let you confidently skip all the usual controls
variants.explanation: Co-localizing reporter and marker confirms targeting.

sources.note: Uses RNAscope to confirm DRG subtype markers for colon afferents.

reviewNotes: Reading co-expression; ties to Cre-line validation.
